---
title: "Assessment"
---

The assessment architecture keeps as much grading as possible automated while preserving human judgement for critique and defence.

| Assessment | Weight | Type | AI/intelligent-tool status | Primary grading mode |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Weekly quizzes | 20% | Individual | Open-resource, time-limited | Canvas auto-graded |
| Studio Critique Portfolio | 15% | Individual | AI-restricted, supervised | Short rubric |
| Tableau Dashboard Checkpoint | 10% | Individual | Allowed with declaration | Checklist + sample moderation |
| Public Data Product Checkpoint | 15% | Group | AI-integrated, documented | Autograder/checklist |
| Group Streamlit App | 20% | Group | AI-integrated, provenance required | Rubric + automated checks |
| Visualisation Quality Review | 10% | Group | AI-integrated, structured review | Structured rubric |
| Individual Oral Defence | 10% | Individual | AI-restricted, live | Human rubric |

## Required disclosure

Every group project must include:

- a user story map,
- a Visual Vocabulary planning table,
- a Data and AI Disclosure,
- an AI Provenance Matrix,
- a revision log after quality review.

## Key rubric principle

Students receive credit not for making the most elaborate visualisation, but for matching visual form to user task and defending the interpretation responsibly.
